description: §6.6.19 TRANSITIVE-limb over-fire guard — a derived cell calling a purely-client local function still compiles, and so does a purely-client mutual-recursion CYCLE in the same file. The transitive limb keys on route inference's settled server PLACEMENT, never on the presence of a call from a derived RHS.
rationale: Over-refusal is the failure mode this shape invites: a derived cell calling a local helper is the ordinary result of extracting logic into a `function`, and refusing it would make §6.6.19 reject the single most common correct use of the derived position. The `alpha`/`beta` cycle is deliberate — the server-reach closure walks the call graph, so a cycle with no server placement in it must both TERMINATE (a stack overflow is not a diagnostic) and stay clean. This is the transitive limb's counterpart to the `-neg` case that pins the direct limb against `scrml:data`: both say the rule keys on the escalation/placement answer and on nothing that merely looks like it.
